- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.67) — model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (especially <0.33) — model fails to capture downside risk or mean reversion.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast when recent history shows mean reversion or downward momentum — model often overreacts to short-term sentiment.
- Correct for lagged mean reversion: if 3–5 days of price decline precede forecast, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to overfit recent highs — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 7-day high to avoid over-optimism.
- Forecast should not exceed 3–5% above 14-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish — avoid “overbought” extrapolation.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a spike, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day to reflect cooling momentum — model often ignores sentiment decay.
